tip: Super + K lists every keybinding on this machine in a menu you can search.
Super + Space opens the Omarchy menu. Start typing to search everything in it.
Super + C and Super + V copy and paste in every app, even terminals, where Ctrl + C would stop the program.
Super + Ctrl + V opens your clipboard history.
Super + Ctrl + R sets a quick reminder; Super + Ctrl + Alt + R shows the ones still waiting.
omarchy reminder 25 "Stretch" sends you a notification in 25 minutes.
Super + Ctrl + I stops the screen from locking or sleeping until you press it again. Handy for talks.
omarchy display text size makes text bigger or smaller everywhere: the shell, apps and terminals.
omarchy theme list shows your themes; omarchy theme set <name> switches to one.
omarchy theme install <git-url> adds a community theme; omarchy theme update keeps them current.
omarchy update takes a system snapshot first, then updates Omarchy and every package.
If an update goes wrong, omarchy snapshot restore rolls the system back to an earlier snapshot.
omarchy pkg install and omarchy pkg remove give you a fuzzy finder over every package.
omarchy launch webapp <url> opens any site in its own app window.
omarchy commands lists the everyday Omarchy commands; add --all to see every one.
omarchy refresh config <path> puts one config file back to the Omarchy default and backs up yours.
omarchy plugin add <git-url> installs a shell plugin; omarchy bar put <id> adds its widget to the bar.
omarchy transcode clip.mov mp4 1080p converts a video for sharing. It handles images too.
Super + Ctrl + 1 to 9 open the panels in the right part of the bar, counted from the left.
omarchy capture qr reads a QR code from a part of the screen and copies what it says.
Print takes a screenshot. While you pick a region, Tab cycles windows and Enter captures the highlighted one.
While picking a screenshot region, Ctrl + Enter captures the whole screen instead.
Super + Ctrl + Print copies the text from any part of the screen (OCR).
Super + Print picks a colour from anywhere on screen and copies it.
Alt + Print opens the screen recording options; press it again to stop recording.
Super + Comma dismisses the latest notification; Super + Shift + Comma clears them all.
Super + Alt + Comma acts on the latest notification, as if you had clicked it.
Super + Ctrl + Comma silences notifications (Do Not Disturb) until you press it again.
Super + Shift + Alt + Comma opens the notification history.
Super + 1 to 9 switch workspace. Add Shift to take the window along, Shift + Alt to send it alone.
Super + Tab steps through workspaces; Super + Ctrl + Tab jumps back to the one you were just on.
Super + Alt + S parks a window in the scratchpad; Super + S shows or hides it.
Super + O pops a window out: floating, and pinned so it follows you across workspaces. Again to tile it.
Super + L switches the workspace between normal tiling and a sideways-scrolling layout.
Super + G turns windows into a tabbed group; Super + Alt + Tab cycles through it.
Super + J flips the split of the focused window between side by side and stacked.
Hold Super and drag with the left mouse button to move a window, with the right button to resize it.
Super + Alt + Home remembers a window's width on this workspace; Super + Home restores it.
Super + Ctrl + Z zooms in on the screen; Super + Ctrl + Alt + Z resets the zoom.
Super + Slash and Super + Alt + Slash step the display scaling up and down.
Super + Shift + Alt + an arrow key moves the whole workspace to the monitor that way.
Super + Return opens a new terminal in the folder of the terminal you are in.
Ctrl + R searches your shell history with fzf: type any part of a command, Enter puts it on the prompt.
Type the start of a command, then press Up: you only step through history that begins the same way.
Ctrl + T pastes a file path picked with fzf; Alt + C jumps into a folder picked the same way.
cd takes partial names: cd proj jumps to the matching folder you visit most (zoxide).
ff is a fuzzy file finder with previews; eff opens the file you pick in your editor.
lt shows the current folder as a tree, two levels deep, with git status.
open <file> opens it in its default app, straight from the terminal.
compress <folder> makes a .tar.gz of it; decompress <file> unpacks one.
n opens Neovim in the current folder; n <file> opens that file.
ga <branch> makes a git worktree for a new branch beside your repo and moves you into it; gd removes it.
fip <host> <port> forwards a remote port to localhost over SSH; lip lists forwards, dip <port> stops one.
tldr <command> shows short, practical examples instead of the whole man page.
Alt + . pastes the last argument of the previous command; press it again to go further back.
Ctrl + X Ctrl + E opens the command you are typing in your editor. Good for long one-liners.
After mkdir new-folder, cd !$ goes into it: !$ is the previous command's last argument.
lazygit is installed: a fast terminal UI for staging hunks, committing and rebasing.
Super + Shift + D opens lazydocker: containers, logs and stats in one view.
watch -d -n 2 <command> reruns it every 2 seconds and highlights what changed.
ss -ltnp shows which program listens on which port; lsof -i :3000 finds the one on port 3000.
command | tee out.log shows the output and saves it to a file at the same time.
journalctl -b -p err shows only the errors logged since this boot.
Super + Alt + Return opens tmux and attaches to your Work session if it is already running.
In tmux the prefix is Ctrl + Space; prefix then ? lists every tmux binding.
In tmux, Alt + Enter splits the pane below, Alt + Shift + Enter beside it, Alt + Escape closes it.
In tmux, Alt + 1 to 9 jumps to a window and Alt + Left or Right steps between windows.
In Neovim, Space Space finds files and Space / searches text across the project.
In Neovim, Space e opens the file explorer and Space g g opens lazygit inside the editor.
In Neovim, press Space and wait: a menu shows every command that can follow.
In Neovim, g d jumps to a definition, K shows its docs and Space c a lists code actions.
In Neovim, Space s k searches all keymaps by name.
git switch - jumps back to the branch you were on before, like cd -.
git commit --fixup <sha>, then git rebase -i --autosquash <base>, folds a fix into the right commit.
git stash push -m "note" -- <file> stashes one file, with a label you can find in git stash list.
git log -S "someFunction" finds the commits that added or removed that text.
git restore --source=main -- <file> takes one file from another branch without switching.
git worktree add ../hotfix main gives you a second checkout, so a hotfix doesn't disturb your branch.
git bisect start, git bisect bad, git bisect good <sha>: git then walks you to the commit that broke it.
git push --force-with-lease is the safe force-push: it refuses if someone else pushed in the meantime.
git diff --stat main...HEAD shows which files your branch changed since it left main.
Omarchy's git config turns on rerere: resolve a merge conflict once and git reuses that fix next time.
The first git push of a new branch sets its upstream for you (push.autoSetupRemote in Omarchy's git config).
git branch lists the most recently committed branches first, thanks to Omarchy's git config.
node --watch app.js restarts on every file change, no nodemon needed.
npm run on its own lists the scripts in package.json; npm explain <package> shows why it is installed.
In psql, \x auto shows wide rows vertically and \timing shows how long each query takes.
EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) shows a query's real plan; a Seq Scan on a big table often means a missing index.
Before a break, write down the very next step. Getting back in takes seconds instead of minutes.
Batch email and chat into two or three fixed slots a day instead of answering each message as it lands.
